query: What diet changes would most effectively lower my blood pressure without medication?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Mayo Clinic, Rochester MN USA): The DASH diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) is the most evidence-based dietary intervention for lowering blood pressure — it reduces systolic BP by 8–14 mmHg in clinical trials through reduced sodium and increased potassium, magnesium, and fiber.

Source 2 (2022, NEJM, Boston MA USA): Sodium restriction to below 2,300 mg/day reduces systolic blood pressure by 5–6 mmHg on average; combined with the DASH diet, the reduction can reach 11–12 mmHg — comparable to a single antihypertensive medication.

Source 3 (2023, WebMD, Atlanta GA USA): Regular aerobic exercise (150 minutes/week) reduces systolic BP by 5–8 mmHg on average and is recommended alongside dietary changes — the combination of DASH, sodium reduction, and exercise can reduce BP by 20+ mmHg.

Source 4 (2022, Reddit r/hypertension, USA): Community reports strong results with the DASH diet combined with sodium tracking — many members reduced BP into normal range within 4–8 weeks without medication; others found strict adherence difficult long-term.

Source 5 (2021, JAMA Internal Medicine, Chicago IL USA): Plant-based diets and Mediterranean-style eating patterns show comparable BP reduction to DASH — dietary pattern consistency matters more than strict adherence to any single named diet.
atoms: perspective: Patient who has tried and failed strict diets
perspective: Patient with stage 1 hypertension seeking non-pharmacological management
plausible_answers: Follow the DASH diet with sodium below 2,300 mg/day, since this produces 8–14 mmHg reduction equivalent to a medication dose.
Focus solely on sodium as the single most impactful lever, since it's easier to track and delivers 5–6 mmHg reduction.
Adopt a Mediterranean diet with 150 minutes weekly aerobic exercise, since this sustainable combination produces comparable long-term BP reduction.
